How Bees Build Hives

Honeybees build their hives from wax secreted by special glands, shaping it into hexagonal cells, which is remarkably efficient.

Each cell serves several purposes, from storing honey and pollen to raising the next generation of workers, drones, and queens.

The geometry is no accident: hexagons use the least wax to enclose the most space, a fact noted by ancient mathematicians.
